The Files and DuckDB module opens a fold: The Files and DuckDB module opens a folder (each CSV, TSV, JSON, Parquet and Excel file in it is a table named after the file), files separated by ;, or a .duckdb database. Join files with SQL as tables of one database. Nexo only reads these files, without network or extensions; the reader settings (delimiter, header, sheet…) are in Driver settings.
The Cassandra module connects to Cassand: The Cassandra module connects to Cassandra and ScyllaDB: write several contact points separated by commas, the keyspace as the database and the local data center in Driver settings. Write CQL in the SQL editor; CONSISTENCY QUORUM and TRACING ON work as in cqlsh, and a query with ALLOW FILTERING asks first, because it may read the whole cluster. In a table's Data tab, filter by the partition key, or add ALLOW FILTERING when Cassandra asks for it.
The Redis module connects to Redis and V: The Redis module connects to Redis and Valkey (one server, Sentinel or a cluster). Open a database of the tree to see its keys by pages, grouped by :, with a pattern and a type to filter them; a key's sheet changes its value, expiry and name. The Console runs commands as redis-cli, with ↑ ↓ for the history; FLUSHDB and the other dangerous ones ask for their name typed. Follow channels in the realtime panel with Redis subscription.
The Elasticsearch module connects to Ela: The Elasticsearch module connects to Elasticsearch and OpenSearch: write the nodes separated by commas and choose basic, apiKey or bearer in Driver settings. Indices show their fields; SQL runs in the SQL editor and in the Data tab of an index. Query DSL console, in the menu of the connection, runs requests as in Kibana: METHOD path and its JSON body, Ctrl+Enter for the one at the cursor. Deleting an index asks for its name typed.
The Apache Drill module connects to a Dr: The Apache Drill module connects to a Drillbit through its REST API (port 8047). Its storage plugins show their schemas, tables and files; query a file as a table, such as dfs.`/data/sales.parquet`. Each page of a result runs the statement again, and values go in the statement, without parameters.

Database tasks (▶ in the navigator) save: Database tasks (▶ in the navigator) save SQL scripts on some connections, a copy of a query into a table of another connection, a comparison of two schemas or tables, a backup or other tasks in order. Run one now or every few minutes or hours while Nexo is open: each run stays in its history, and a failure or a difference found is notified. Nobody confirms a scheduled run, so what would ask (changes in production, statements on every row, DROP) runs only if the task authorizes it.
nx.sql('Shop') reads and changes a saved: nx.sql('Shop') reads and changes a saved SQL connection from a script: query(sql, params) gives up to 1,000 rows as objects by column, queryOne the first one, execute a change (add { confirm: true } where the SQL editor would ask), and transaction(fn) commits it or undoes it if it throws. Parameters are always bound, with the markers of the engine ($1, ?, @p1). Each run of the script has its own session, closed when it ends; the script never sees the address or the password.
With Let MCP agents read it in the Gener: With Let MCP agents read it in the General tab of a SQL connection, agents get sql_list_tables, sql_describe_table, sql_query (only statements that read, 100 rows at most) and sql_explain, each call on a session that only reads. The columns you list there (users.password, *_token) come as [hidden], also under another name.

It reads the connection from the DATABASE_URL environment variable. Copy as string gives the statement alone as a string of that language, and Paste from code turns a string copied from a program back into SQL.
